app.name: Echo
app.tagline: Know your rights. Get help safely.
demo.banner: Demo version · Information only, not legal advice
exit.label: Exit
exit.aria: Quick exit: switch to a different screen
sos.label: SOS
home.intro: You can tell me what is happening at work, in your own words. I'll explain your rights under Singapore's rules and help you find support. What you share stays on this phone.
home.privacyNote: Echo doesn't use accounts or tracking. Tap Exit at any time to hide this app instantly.
chat.disclaimer: Echo gives information, not legal advice.
chat.fallback: The AI model was unavailable, so Echo used its on-device checks.
reply.mild: Thanks for asking. Here is what the rules say about this.
reply.moderate: I'm sorry you're dealing with this. From what you describe, this may go against MOM's rules. Here is what the rules say, and some steps you can take whenever you're ready.
reply.serious: Thank you for telling me. What you describe sounds serious, and it's not your fault. Here is what the rules say, and some options you can take at your own pace.
reply.crisis: I'm really sorry. Your safety matters most right now. I've opened the emergency contacts. If you are in danger, please call 999.
reply.notReady: That's completely okay. You don't have to do anything right now. I've saved the information below so it's here whenever you want it.
reply.noMatch: I couldn't find a specific rule about this in my knowledge base. You could try describing it in other words, or ask CDE for advice. They are open 24 hours.
actions.title: What you can do
actions.moderate.1: Write down what happened, with dates. Keep photos of salary records or messages.
actions.moderate.2: If you feel safe, you can talk to your employer about the rule.
actions.moderate.3: If you want help, you can contact MOM or CDE. You can also report online on MOM's website.
actions.serious.1: If you can, keep your phone and important documents somewhere safe that you can reach.
actions.serious.2: Write down what happened, with dates, and keep any messages or photos.
actions.serious.3: Before deciding to leave, talk to CDE or HOME. They can explain your options safely.
actions.serious.4: You can report to MOM online or by phone whenever you are ready.
actions.journalSoon: Coming soon: the encrypted, on-device journal.
saved.title: Saved for later
saved.note: Kept on this screen only. Cleared when you tap Exit.
signal.confinement: being locked in or not allowed to leave
signal.self-harm: thoughts of ending your life or hurting yourself
signal.denied-food-or-care: being denied food or medical care
signal.passport-held: your passport or documents being kept
signal.isolated: being cut off from your phone or family
signal.overwork: very long hours or too little sleep
emergency.title: Get help now
emergency.crisisTitle: You don't have to face this alone
emergency.intro: If you are in danger, call the Police first. You are not in trouble for asking for help.
emergency.control: You stay in control. You can call just to talk or ask for advice, and you decide what happens next.
emergency.notReady: I'm not ready to call yet. Take me back
emergency.unverified: Not yet verified. Please check this number before relying on it.
contact.police.desc: If you are in danger or someone is hurting you.
contact.ambulance.desc: If you or someone else is badly hurt or very sick.
contact.cde.desc: Help with problems at work: salary, rest days, how you are treated.
contact.home.desc: Support and advice from a charity for migrant workers. Call or WhatsApp.
contact.mom.desc: Speak to a Ministry of Manpower officer if you are in distress.
contact.sos.desc: Someone to talk to if you feel hopeless or are thinking of ending your life.
